content: 1. Administer metoclopramide intravenously at a dose of 1-2 mg/kg every 6-8 hours as needed. When used for chemotherapy-induced nausea, infuse the dose over at least 15 minutes, 30 minutes prior to chemotherapy. Repeat every 2-4 hours as necessary. Pretreatment with diphenhydramine can reduce the risk of extrapyramidal side effects. 2. Metoclopramide increases the toxicity of lurasidone due to its antidopaminergic effects, which may result in extrapyramidal symptoms or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. This combination is contraindicated. 3. The concurrent use of metoclopramide and antipsychotics is contraindicated due to an increased risk of extrapyramidal effects, as per the manufacturer’s guidelines. 4. Metoclopramide reduces the levels of cabergoline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, metoclopramide decreases cabergoline levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Metoclopramide and citalopram both increase serotonin levels, leading to additive effects and an increased risk of serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, dystonia, or other extrapyramidal reactions. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Metoclopramide and desvenlafaxine both elevate serotonin levels, resulting in additive effects and a heightened risk of serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, dystonia, or other extrapyramidal reactions. Avoid this combination or consider an alternative therapy. 7. Metoclopramide decreases dopamine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, metoclopramide reduces dopamine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Avoid this combination or consider an alternative therapy. 12. Metoclopramide decreases the effects of inhaled levodopa through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists should not be coadministered with inhaled levodopa. 13. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, metoclopramide decreases lisuride levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Additionally, metoclopramide decreases methyldopa levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Avoid this combination or consider an alternative therapy. 17. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Metoclopramide decreases the levels of pramipexole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Metoclopramide increases the levels of red yeast rice by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. This interaction may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, as red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. 20. Rivastigmine and metoclopramide both increase the toxicity of each other through antidopaminergic effects, including extrapyramidal symptoms and neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
